newsitem.title: USA: Merged Brooklyn Union, Lilco payout seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Merged Brooklyn Union, Lilco payout seen higher.

text.p: Brooklyn Union Gas Co said the proxy describing its proposed merger with Long Island Lighting Co states the initial annualized dividend rate for the common stock of the new holding company resulting from the combination is expected to be $1.78 per share.

This is an increase of $0.32 per share and is 22 percent higher than the current Brooklyn Union dividend rate of $1.46, the company said. Its shareholders will get one share of the new company for each share now held.

Lilco holders, who will get 0.88 share of the new company for each share now held -- if its planned sale of assets to the Long Island Power Authority is completed, 0.803 share if the LIPA transaction is not completed -- now receive annual dividend payments of $1.78.
Both companies will hold special shareholder meetings August 7 to approve the proposed combination of the two companies.
In addition, Brooklyn Union shareholders will also be asked to approve the formation of the KeySpan holding company as an interim step for Brooklyn Union prior to the combination, the company said.
Upon shareholder approval, Brooklyn Union explained, KeySpan Energy Corp will be consolidated with Lilco into a separate holding company, yet to be named.
Shareholders of record as of June 26 are eligible to vote.
